page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6r.2xlarge is an Arm-based general-purpose instance powered by a 2.8 GHz Ampere Altra processor. Operating under a KVM hypervisor, the virtual machine provides 8 dedicated physical vCPUs paired with 32.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance configuration includes no bundled local storage, relying on network-attached block storage volumes, and offers a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. Accelerated graphics hardware is absent, with 0 GPUs provisioned on the host.

Performance profiles show a contrast between multi-threaded scalability and single-threaded execution capacity. Multi-core operations register consistently within the median range across synthetic suites, yielding a Geekbench multi-core score of 6111.0, a Clang compilation score of 9358.0, and 14296.73 in stress-ng multi-core testing. Conversely, single-threaded throughput falls into the lower 25% bracket, reflected by a Geekbench single-core result of 1095.0, weak gzip compression throughput of 23.7 GB/sec, and a PassMark CPU score of 6192.59. Memory subsystems demonstrate stable throughput, sustaining 86.12 GB/sec uncached reads and 47.27 GB/sec uncached writes on large 256 MB blocks.

The Arm64 architecture delivers balanced memory density and predictable dedicated compute allocation, rendering the hardware cost-efficient for scale-out distributed systems rather than single-thread bound routines. While execution speeds lag on heavy vector or unoptimized x86 routines, the instance achieves 10.86 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations, alongside 10.65 GB/sec static web serving throughput. Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6r.2xlarge is well matched for Redis caching nodes, microservices hosting, containerized software compilation pipelines, web serving layers, and transactional database tasks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6r.2xlarge is an Arm-based general-purpose server instance configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs from a 2.8 GHz Ampere Altra processor and 32.0 GB of RAM. The instance lacks local storage and dedicated GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage while maintaining a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier multi-threaded capacity, scoring 6111.0 in Geekbench multi-core and processing 10.86 million Redis SET operations per second, alongside 10.65 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. In contrast, single-core execution and compression workloads land in lower percentiles due to architecture trade-offs. The balanced 4.0 GB memory-to-vCPU ratio offers steady resource density for multi-threaded scale-out deployments. The instance is suited for containerized microservices, distributed in-memory caching, web serving, software build clusters, and standard relational database workloads.
